summary.intent: Execute phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) of the CipherBox GSD workflow — hardening IPNS record verification to be strictly fail-closed across Rust (fuse, api-client, sdk) and TypeScript (sdk-core, web) layers, unifying first-publish seq numbers, and routing all resolve paths through a single chokepoint.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 fully complete (plans 60-01, 60-02, 60-03 — 251/251 sdk-core tests passing, fuse check green). Wave 2 plan 60-04 complete. Stray artifacts from Wave 1 executors (uncommitted Cargo.lock and incorrect SUMMARY footer) were caught and cleaned up before Wave 2 continued.

repo: IPNS verification was previously split across crates/fuse/src/verify.rs and crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs; 60-01 centralized it in api-client, and 60-04 deleted the fuse re-export entirely.

VerifyError::Legacy variant was removed as part of the strict fail-closed hardening; all 9 FUSE caller arms migrated to Invalid — this was a compile necessity that 60-01 handled ahead of 60-04's declared scope.
First-publish IPNS records previously embedded sequence=0; unified to sequence=1 across 9 producers (FUSE, desktop Tauri, sdk-core, web) in 60-02.
sdk-core has 251 tests, 34 of which are IPNS-specific — used as the primary integration gate between waves.
Windows winfsp site is CI-gated and not locally testable; expected to show as skipped during local checks.
No git submodules in the repo, so all plans were eligible for worktree isolation — but the orchestrator chose sequential execution due to worktree merge-back complexity.

code.finding: Was using VerifyError::Legacy; migrated to VerifyError::Invalid by 60-01 as part of folding all Legacy caller arms.
Had a stale expectation of 0n for IPNS sequence; updated to 1n as a consequence of 60-02's seq=1 unification.

60-01 added ciborium and cipherbox-core as deps to crates/api-client/Cargo.toml (for CBOR Validity parsing) but the executor never committed the corresponding Cargo.lock update — a latent --locked CI break discovered only in Wave 2.

workflow: GSD executor subagents can emit stale mid-edit diagnostics (e.g., reporting a compile error that was already fixed in the same session) — always re-run cargo check/test authoritatively before marking a plan failed.

Worktree isolation mode for Agent tool is not reliably usable when branches need to be merged back into the feature branch; sequential execution on the shared working tree is safer for complex phases.
Executors don't always commit Cargo.lock alongside Cargo.toml changes — the orchestrator must inspect `git status` between plans to catch uncommitted lockfile drift.
Stray content (summary footers, diagnostic artifacts) can be appended to plan SUMMARY files after the plan's own commit, leaving stale information in the tree that subsequent plans may contradict.

friction: 60-01 executor reported a compile error (VerifyError::Legacy at metadata.rs:619) that was already resolved within the same edit session — required a manual grep and cargo check to confirm the tree was actually green.

Worktree-based parallel execution (the preferred mode) is not reliably supported because there is no exposed worktree path/branch manifest for merge-back, forcing sequential execution and losing wave parallelism.
Cargo.lock was left uncommitted after 60-01's Cargo.toml edits, discovered only mid-Wave 2 via `git status` — would have caused a --locked CI failure.
60-01-SUMMARY.md had a stale footer appended post-commit (saying 'verify.rs FOUND') that contradicted 60-04's deletion — required manual revert.
open_items: Wave 2 plans 60-05 (tighten API regime) and 60-07 (regen cross-lang test vectors) not yet executed — transcript ends after 60-04 cleanup.
Wave 3 plan 60-06 (API publish-path verify cache for CPU cost recovery) not started.
Wave 4 plan 60-08 (D-01/D-12 operational cutover: staging wipe + redeploy + smoke-test) is non-autonomous and requires a human-action checkpoint — not yet reached.
